original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A municipal test finds contamination in one water-supply line. The report says the line must not be used until a new test clears it. Which actions should the authority take? Actions: I. Stop supply from the affected line and provide a tested alternative. II. Issue a notice advising residents not to drink water from that line until it is cleared.

options.A: Both actions I and II follow
options.C: Only action II follows
options.E: Either action I or II follows

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both actions I and II follow
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both actions immediately protect residents while respecting the test condition.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A public examination hall has more candidates at its entrance than the safe occupancy limit. Which actions should the invigilator take? Actions: I. Pause entry and move candidates to an available approved hall. II. Admit everyone quickly so the exam can start on time.

options.C: Both actions I and II follow
options.E: Either action I or II follows

original_practice_entries.explanation: Only I maintains the stated safety limit; speed does not justify exceeding occupancy.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A bank detects that several customers entered passwords on a confirmed phishing page. Which actions are appropriate? Actions: I. Require affected customers to reset credentials through the official channel. II. Warn customers and strengthen monitoring for suspicious account activity.

options.C: Both actions I and II follow
options.E: Either action I or II follows

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both actions I and II follow
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both actions directly reduce the risk from credentials already exposed.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — An inspection reports that a bridge support is structurally unsafe until repaired. Which actions should the local authority take? Actions: I. Close the bridge to traffic. II. Mark the closure and direct traffic to a safe alternative route.

options.C: Only action II follows
options.D: Both actions I and II follow
options.E: Either action I or II follows

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both actions I and II follow
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both closure and clear diversion are needed to prevent use and guide road users.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A library's audit finds that books are leaving without a recorded checkout. Which actions are suitable? Actions: I. Review access and checkout records to locate the control failure. II. Add an exit check that verifies each book against a recorded loan.

options.A: Either action I or II follows
options.C: Only action II follows
options.E: Both actions I and II follow

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both actions I and II follow
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both actions investigate the current failure and prevent recurrence.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A rural clinic reports that vaccination appointments are being missed because the nearest center is several hours away. Which actions should the health office take? Actions: I. Arrange temporary outreach sessions closer to the affected villages. II. Map missed appointments and contact residents with the new session details.

options.A: Both actions I and II follow
options.C: Only action II follows
options.E: Either action I or II follows

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both actions I and II follow
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both measures address access and help the intended residents use the service.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A logged short circuit disabled circuit C at 10:05. A machine connected only to C stopped at 10:06, and its log records loss of power as the reason. Statements: I. The machine stopped. II. Circuit C suffered a short circuit.

options.A: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.B: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.C: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.D: The events are stated to be unrelated
options.E: The order alone does not establish a causal link

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: II is the cause and I is its effect
original_practice_entries.explanation: The short circuit (II) removed the machine's power; the machine stopping (I) followed.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A pump failed at 08:00. The building's water pressure fell immediately afterward, and the maintenance report confirms the pump was the sole source of pressure. Statements: I. Water pressure fell. II. The pump failed.

options.A: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.B: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.C: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.D: The events are stated to be unrelated
options.E: The order alone does not establish a causal link

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: II is the cause and I is its effect
original_practice_entries.explanation: The documented pump failure (II) caused the pressure drop (I).
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — An overnight frost damaged the orchard's blossoms. The same frost also froze an exposed irrigation pipe; the report identifies the frost as the cause of both events. Statements: I. Orchard blossoms were damaged. II. An exposed irrigation pipe froze.

options.A: The events are stated to be unrelated
options.B: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.C: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.D: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.E: The order alone does not establish a causal link

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: Both are effects of the same stated cause
original_practice_entries.explanation: Both events are explicitly attributed to the overnight frost, a common cause.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A station closed its east entrance for repairs. A separate power fault at another station was traced to a damaged transformer, and the inspection confirms the incidents are unrelated. Statements: I. The east entrance closed. II. Power failed at the other station.

options.A: The order alone does not establish a causal link
options.B: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.C: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.D: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.E: The events are stated to be unrelated

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: The events are stated to be unrelated
original_practice_entries.explanation: The report explicitly says the two incidents have unrelated causes.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A delivery vehicle arrived late. The dispatch record shows it left on time, while a road closure on its route added forty minutes; the receiving office opened at its normal time. Statements: I. The vehicle arrived late. II. A road closure added forty minutes to its route.

options.A: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.B: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.C: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.D: The events are stated to be unrelated
options.E: The order alone does not establish a causal link

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: I is the cause and II is its effect
original_practice_entries.explanation: The closure (II) added travel time and caused the late arrival (I).
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A heating unit shut down after its thermostat sensor failed. The repair log confirms the failed sensor triggered the unit's safety shutdown. Statements: I. The thermostat sensor failed. II. The heating unit shut down.

options.A: II is the cause and I is its effect
options.B: I is the cause and II is its effect
options.C: Both are effects of the same stated cause
options.D: The events are stated to be unrelated
options.E: The order alone does not establish a causal link

original_practice_entries.correct_answer: I is the cause and II is its effect
original_practice_entries.explanation: The failed sensor (I) triggered the shutdown (II).
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A bank introduces a mobile queue-token service to reduce the time customers spend waiting at branches. Assumptions: I. Queue management contributes to customer waiting time. II. Every customer owns a smartphone.

options.A: Both assumptions I and II are implicit
options.C: Only assumption I is implicit
options.E: Either assumption I or II is implicit

original_practice_entries.explanation: The stated purpose assumes queue management affects waiting; it does not require every customer to own a smartphone because alternatives may exist.
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — The city will add evening bus trips on the route after passenger counts show heavy crowding during that period. Assumptions: I. Some passengers would use additional evening trips. II. The route has no passengers at other times.

options.E: Either assumption I or II is implicit

original_practice_entries.explanation: Additional trips can address crowding only if there is demand for them; nothing assumes the route is empty at other times.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — All approved applications were reviewed by two officers. Some applications reviewed by two officers were returned for correction. options.C: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.E: Either conclusion I or II follows

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A scholarship is granted only if the applicant has at least 80% attendance, a pass in every subject, and household income below ₹4 lakh. options.C: Charu only
options.E: Asha only

original_practice_entries.explanation: Asha satisfies all three thresholds. Bharat exceeds the income limit, and Charu did not pass every subject.
